subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which mineral-carrying tissue is also important in supporting the plant?
questions.explain: Lignified xylem vessels help support the plant as well as transporting water.

questions.q: Which tissue transports water and mineral ions up the plant?
questions.explain: Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals upwards from the roots.

options: The continuous movement of water from roots up through the xylem to the leaves
The flow of sugars in phloem
Water draining out of the soil
The movement of air through stomata
questions.explain: As water evaporates from leaves, more is pulled up through the xylem in the transpiration stream.

questions.q: Which change would INCREASE the rate of diffusion?
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more kinetic energy, increasing diffusion rate; larger surface area, steeper gradient and shorter distance also help.

options: Water from a dilute to a more concentrated solution through a partially permeable membrane
Particles from high to low concentration using ATP
Any dissolved solute across a membrane
Water from a concentrated to a dilute solution
questions.explain: Osmosis is the diffusion of water only, from a dilute (high water) to a more concentrated (low water) solution through a partially permeable membrane.

questions.q: A cell placed in a concentrated salt solution loses water and shrinks. This is because water moves:
options: Out of the cell by osmosis down its water gradient
Out of the cell by active transport
Into the cell by diffusion of salt
questions.explain: The salt solution has a lower water concentration, so water leaves the cell by osmosis.

questions.q: Why does increased light intensity tend to increase transpiration?
options: Stomata open in the light for photosynthesis, allowing more water to escape
questions.explain: In light, stomata open to allow gas exchange for photosynthesis, so more water vapour is lost.

questions.q: Which statement about xylem is correct?
options: It is made of dead cells strengthened with lignin and carries water
It is made of living cells and carries sugars
It transports food in both directions
questions.explain: Xylem vessels are dead, hollow tubes strengthened by lignin that carry water upwards.

questions.q: The movement of sugars through phloem is called...
questions.explain: Translocation is the transport of dissolved food (sucrose) in the phloem.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes phloem from xylem?
options: Phloem is made of living cells
Phloem is made of dead cells
questions.explain: Phloem is composed of living cells, unlike the dead xylem vessels.

options: The movement of sugars in phloem
The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant
questions.explain: Transpiration is the evaporation and loss of water vapour, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.q: Why do single-celled organisms NOT need a transport system?
options: They have a large surface area to volume ratio so diffusion is sufficient
They use active transport for everything
questions.explain: Their large surface area to volume ratio and short diffusion distances allow exchange by diffusion alone.
